desc: Ideation and problem analysis (deriving the single-component nested backward matching structure).
Recognize that the outermost chord must be B@1 → W@2N, with S[1]='B' and S[2N]='W'.
Recognize that inside, we recursively find a non-crossing backward matching forming a single nested component.
Conjecture: the number of valid pairings is computed by a divide-and-conquer DP over intervals.
Implement the divide-and-conquer recursion (current O(N^2) worst case code).

Optimize to O(N) using a stack-based DP: treat B as '(', W as ')' on a line; use a stack of unmatched B positions; for each W, either match with the closest unmatched B to its left (closing a sub-cycle) or with a deeper B to start a new outer cycle. Maintain dp over the number of unmatched B's and use prefix sums for O(1) transitions.
Test the optimized implementation against the three sample inputs (N=2 BWBW → 1; N=4 BWWBWBWB → 0; N=9 BWWBWBBBWWBWBBWWBW → 240792).
Verify correctness on edge cases (N=1, all B's then all W's, alternating patterns, large N up to 2×10^5).
Final review: ensure O(N) time, O(N) memory, correct modulo arithmetic, no off-by-one errors, submit final code.
